paper_metadata.title: Variational Quantum Circuit-Based Reinforcement Learning for Dynamic Portfolio Optimization

summary: The paper proposes variational quantum circuit reinforcement learning (QRL) for dynamic portfolio optimization over 15 assets using real market data (2011–2025). The best quantum model (Quantum DDPG with 60 parameters) achieved a Sharpe ratio of 0.7281, while the best classical baseline (DQN with 160k parameters) achieved 0.8237, indicating comparable but not superior performance with far fewer parameters.

experiments.description: Quantum DDPG for dynamic portfolio optimization using a variational quantum circuit actor-critic architecture, trained on a noiseless statevector simulator and deployed for inference on IBM Eagle r3 superconducting hardware.

algorithm.variant: Quantum DDPG with VQC actor and VQC critic
algorithm.ansatz: parameterized variational quantum circuit with alternating single-qubit rotations and entangling gates; amplitude-encoded feature map plus trainable layers

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical financial state is normalized, expanded with feature map Z(x)=[x, x⊙2, sin(x), cos(x)], then amplitude-encoded; first N qubits are measured and ℓ1-normalized to portfolio weights
problem_formulation.objective_function: maximize risk-adjusted portfolio return over time; reward rt = w_t^T μ_{t-L:t+F+1} - η w_t^T Σ_{t-L:t+F+1} w_t
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: portfolio weights are ℓ1-normalized to satisfy full-investment constraint; short selling permitted up to 100% of initial portfolio value

problem_instance.description: Dynamic portfolio optimization over 15 assets with 30-day lookback and 7-day forecast, rebalanced every 30 days

dataset_specification.preprocessing: logarithmic returns from daily closing prices; normalized asset prices; 7-day Auto ARIMA forecast appended to state
dataset_specification.train_test_split: 7-fold increasing rolling-window time-series cross-validation with training/validation/test splits

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: daily closing prices converted to log returns; 30-day rolling normalized price window; 7-day Auto ARIMA forecast; transaction costs of 0.15% per trade included in evaluation
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 7-fold expanding-window time-series cross-validation; mean and standard deviation of Sharpe ratio across folds

implementation_details.classical_solver: Adam/SGD for training; no separate classical optimization solver reported
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Bayesian hyperparameter search; statevector simulation for training; Auto ARIMA forecasting; transaction cost modeling
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Pauli-Z expectation values converted to marginal probabilities and ℓ1-normalized into portfolio weights
implementation_details.total_execution_time: 23 minutes cloud job duration for QPU inference
implementation_details.quantum_execution_time: < 1 s per circuit execution reported at circuit level; ~12 s per forward pass on cloud QPU

results.unit: seconds per circuit execution (reported as < 1 s)
seconds per forward pass on cloud QPU

speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical deep rl and classical portfolio baselines
speedup_claims.conditions: current noisy cloud-based quantum deployment; finite-shot inference on IBM Eagle r3
speedup_claims.caveats: Paper emphasizes parameter efficiency and comparable risk-adjusted performance, but does not claim or demonstrate an asymptotic quantum speedup. End-to-end latency is dominated by cloud overhead.

complexity_analysis.wall_clock_quantum: < 1 s circuit execution; 23 min cloud job duration
complexity_analysis.wall_clock_classical: 7 s for classical DDPG with 13.5k params; 14 s for classical DDPG with 160k params

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Paper does not provide asymptotic complexity or scaling evidence; experiments limited to VQCs with ≤60 parameters and circuits small enough to run on ~20 qubits.
limiting_factors: Best classical Sharpe ratio (0.8237) exceeds quantum results
Training performed only on statevector simulator
Small circuit size and limited qubit counts
Amplitude encoding requires expensive state preparation scaling O(2^n)
Cloud QPU latency dominates end‑to‑end runtime

notes: num_qubits not explicitly stated for the QRL circuit; inferred as not directly reported because the paper only states amplitude encoding uses O(log d) qubits and that available GPU limited circuit width to roughly 20 qubits, but no exact circuit width for the deployed model is given.
speedup_order inferred as none_proven because the paper discusses practical latency and parameter efficiency but does not claim an asymptotic quantum speedup.
Authors state quantum agents achieve comparable performance with fewer parameters but explicitly note that classical models still achieve higher Sharpe ratios in their experiments.
